rounds.fact: LAUNCH (later LAUNCHcast) was one of Yahoo's earliest music properties, offering personalized internet radio years before Pandora or Spotify existed.
Expedia started in 1996 as a project inside Microsoft before spinning off into its own company, part of the first wave of travel booking moving from agents onto the web.
Ask Jeeves branded itself around a friendly butler mascot and the pitch of asking questions in plain English, a contrast to the keyword-heavy search engines of the era.
CNET launched in 1994 as one of the first tech-focused media companies built for the web, eventually growing to include Download.com and several other well-known tech properties.
Bebo was massively popular in the UK and Ireland during the mid-2000s, at one point ranking as the third-most-visited social network in the US before AOL bought it for $850 million in 2008.
